purpose: Fresh concrete Agent Skills alternative to the October 8 Gemini Skills article that overlaps the October 9 edition; editorial producer must independently decide selection and preserve exact-one-skills rule.
headline_candidate: PayPal puts reusable Agent Skills through a human-reviewed trust pipeline

source.title: How PayPal is governing agent skills at enterprise scale

read_evidence.scope: Complete original PayPal October 9 article, including skill package structure, team-owned GitHub repositories, read-only registry discovery and webhooks, blocking security validation, human approval, versioned marketplace release, and future Agent Plugins roadmap.

mechanism: A team packages reusable instructions in SKILL.md and optional references, scripts, and assets in its own GitHub repository. A read-only GitHub App discovers new or changed packages. Each submission passes structure, sensitive-data, harmful-instructions and prompt-injection checks, with duplication advisory, then an administrator approves the version for marketplace distribution. Every revision enters the same review path.
concrete_practitioner_value: Use one reusable skill folder for a bounded recurring work procedure; keep source ownership in the functional team; require security checks and an authorized human reviewer for every version before wide distribution.
caveats: PayPal's own design statement; not independently evaluated for effectiveness or security.
Plugin packaging for roles is a future plan, not established current availability.
LangChain and Snyk percentages cited by PayPal are third-party claims; avoid repeating without independent validation.
cross_edition_overlap: Different from October 9 Gemini modular-skill announcement: focuses on internal package governance, read-only repository intake, blocking validation, versioning and human approval.
